verifiedAgainst.note: Verified: project-scoped MCP servers live in a `.mcp.json` at the project root, checked into version control, in the standardized shape {"mcpServers": {"<name>": {...}}}. A stdio server carries command/args/env; an http server carries type and url. THE FILE FORMAT IS VERIFIED; THE CONTENT MODEL IS NOT VENDOR-SPECIFIED. docs/SPEC.md section 10.9 asks for 'an MCP server manifest' without saying what a document-derived one should contain, so what this target puts inside the verified envelope is our design and is described in vendorFields.

vendorFields.contentModel: One server entry. Its command and args are template scaffolding, declared here and therefore exempt from the traceability gate exactly as a Markdown heading is. Its `env` block is the only unit-derived part: one key per environmentVariable unit, each traceable to the unit and through it to a source locator. Nothing in this file is prose, so the gate runs over derived key/value pairs rather than over segmented sentences.
vendorFields.honestyNote: The server this manifest points at now exists: `markforge mcp`, an stdio MCP server exposing convert, fmt, and agentify. Corrected on 2026-08-01, and the correction is worth recording because this field was wrong about its own profile in three ways at once. It said the manifest named `markforge serve` — the scaffold above actually said `npx -y @markforge/mcp`, which is not the same command; `markforge serve` is the HTTP API and would hang if an MCP client spawned it on stdio; and `npx @markforge/mcp` names a package nothing publishes and nothing may publish (OPEN_QUESTIONS section 5), so the scaffold could not have worked from any checkout. The dropped `--context .markforge/provenance.json` argument was a flag no server ever accepted. STATUS.md and docs/TARGETS.md both repeated the `markforge serve` claim, inheriting the error from here.
